subject: Community Resilience Hubs
overview: Panelists from Medford, Baltimore, and the Clean Energy Group discussed strategies for developing community resilience hubs during an Accelerating Climate Resilience webinar. The conversation focused on network-based operational models, clean energy backup systems, equity-focused engagement, and grant funding opportunities.

items.title: Welcome and Panelist Introductions
items.summary: The Metropolitan Area Planning Council opened the Accelerating Climate Resilience speaker series event featuring municipal planners and energy resilience experts.

items.title: Defining Resilience Hubs in Medford and Baltimore
items.summary: Penelope Funaiole described Medford's network-based approach using trusted city services and multilingual liaisons, while Aubrey Germ detailed Baltimore's partnership model with hyper-local nonprofits.

items.title: Energy Resilience and Solar Storage Capabilities
items.summary: Abby Ramana highlighted how solar and battery storage systems ensure continuous facility operations during power outages while offering bill savings during normal grid operation.

items.title: Resilient Power Technical Assistance Fund
items.summary: Abby Ramana explained how Clean Energy Group provides pre-development feasibility grants to assist community institutions in designing solar and storage projects.

items.title: Building Trust and Multilingual Community Engagement
items.summary: Panelists detailed strategies for establishing long-term trust, utilizing paid language liaisons, and simplifying outreach language to effectively engage vulnerable residents.

items.title: Funding Opportunities and Future Resilience Outlook
items.summary: Panelists discussed leveraging federal Inflation Reduction Act incentives and FEMA mitigation grants to expand local climate resilience hub infrastructure.
